::: {#lem-bfs-order}
#### Breadth-first search removes vertices in order of their labels

Let $G$ and $s$ be as in @def-bfs.
Then `bfs(G, s)` removes the vertices from its queue (@def-queue) with their labels $\texttt{dist}$ in nondecreasing order.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Let $I$ be the statement that,
if $x_1, \ldots, x_k$ are the vertices in the queue $Q$ from front to back, then

$$
\texttt{dist}[x_1] \le \texttt{dist}[x_2] \le \cdots \le \texttt{dist}[x_k] \le \texttt{dist}[x_1] + 1.
$$

**$I$ holds at the first test of the loop.**
Then $Q$ holds only $s$, and $\texttt{dist}[s] \le \texttt{dist}[s] + 1$.

**$I$ is a loop invariant.**
Suppose $I$ holds at a test, and the pass removes $v = x_1$.
The vertices $x_2, \ldots, x_k$ that remain have labels in nondecreasing order,
each from $\texttt{dist}[v]$ to $\texttt{dist}[v] + 1$.
Every vertex the pass adds goes to the back, with the label $\texttt{dist}[v] + 1$,
which is at least every label before it.
So the labels in $Q$ are still in nondecreasing order.
Each of them is at most $\texttt{dist}[v] + 1$,
and the new first label is at least $\texttt{dist}[v]$,
so the last label is at most the new first label plus 1.
So $I$ holds at the next test, and $I$ is a loop invariant, by @thm-loop-invariant.

**The labels never decrease.**
Suppose a pass removes $v$, and the next pass removes $w$.
At the test between them, $I$ holds, and $w$ is at the front of $Q$.
Every label in $Q$ at that test is either the label of a vertex that was behind $v$, which is at least $\texttt{dist}[v]$ by $I$ before the pass,
or $\texttt{dist}[v] + 1$.
So $\texttt{dist}[w] \ge \texttt{dist}[v]$.

:::

:::
